judged_text: Office365 refresh no longer checks `tokenResponse.success` before persisting credentials; minimum schema may return data missing `expiry_date`, persisting stale credentials and defeating the refresh loop

record.issue_text: Office365 refresh no longer checks `tokenResponse.success` before persisting credentials; minimum schema may return data missing `expiry_date`, persisting stale credentials and defeating the refresh loop

adjudication.rationale: In `Office365CalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not require `expiry_date` (and does not map any numeric expiry field into `expiry_date`). That means the refreshed credential can be persisted without updating `expiry_date`, leaving the old/stale expiry value in place and potentially causing repeated refreshes or incorrect expiry handling. The finding’s statement about not checking `tokenResponse.success` is slightly off because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on unsuccessful parse, but the underlying issue about missing `expiry_date` being allowed is grounded in the diff.
